Do not assume the conference’s exhibition, catering or networking spend will move from campus to this hotel. Breakfast-only options merit discussion because delegates may spend conference days away from the resort.

establishedFacts: The official event site announces 21–23 April 2027, One Health, St. George’s University campus in Grenada, with CARPHA, the ministry and SGU as joint hosts.
The conference has advertised sponsorship and exhibition opportunities; the exhibition offer includes face-to-face delegate engagement and a coffee break in the exhibition area.
CARPHA reports preparatory discussions with SGU about conference logistics and stakeholder engagement.
Spice Island’s official accommodation inventory is 64 luxury villa-style suites; its resort page lists all-day dining with breakfast-only options available.
The resort advertises full-service wedding/event staff and catering for up to 35 guests in its wedding offer; no general conference capacity was established.
The accommodation page’s linked flyer is for the 2026 Guyana edition and must not be treated as a 2027 Grenada hotel list.
uncertainties: No verified hotel-sourcing or contracting decision-maker; all named contacts are planners, commercial-administration contacts, influencers or referrals rather than confirmed hotel buyers.
Roxanne Colthrust’s and Veron Guy-Parks’s documented conference responsibilities relate to 2026; continuation into 2027 is unconfirmed.
No verified 2027 attendance total, accommodation requirement, room-night commitment, budget, rate ceiling or Spice Island allocation.
No evidence that Spice Island is an official, preferred, overflow or contracted conference hotel.
No verified hotel meeting-room inventory, corporate-event capacity, date availability, accessible-suite specifications or campus transport arrangement.
No evidence of an incentive-travel component or a requirement for a resort-wide buyout.
qualificationQuestions: Who owns 2027 accommodation sourcing and who may sign a hotel agreement: CARPHA, SGU, the ministry, an appointed planner or individual delegates?
Is Roxanne Colthrust assigned to the 71st conference, and who is the current operational accommodation lead?
Is there a preferred-hotel list, RFP, room-block deadline or existing exclusive accommodation arrangement?
Which guests require accommodation, on which arrival/departure dates, and is demand organizer-funded or self-booked?
What rate ceilings, payment guarantees, taxes, deposits, release dates and cancellation/attrition terms apply?
Would breakfast-only pricing be preferable to all-inclusive pricing while delegates attend campus sessions?
Are off-campus dinners, receptions or small private meetings planned; what are their headcounts, security and AV needs?
Who arranges SGU transfers, and what accessibility, dietary, medical or protocol requirements must the hotel meet?
snapshot.recommendedNextStep: Send a short, permission-based accommodation enquiry to conference@carpha.org, asking for the named 2027 accommodation/logistics lead and whether CARPHA, SGU, the ministry or individual delegates source and pay for hotels. Ask whether Roxanne Colthrust remains involved; use Veron Guy-Parks as an alternative administrative referral and Rhonda-Joy Lewis for routing if needed. Suggested positioning: “Could you direct us to the person coordinating accommodation for the 21–23 April 2027 conference? Spice Island would like to assess whether a limited suite allocation or small private hospitality event could fit your needs. Please confirm the sourcing process, permitted rate basis and transport requirements.” Only then prepare a tailored proposal with availability, inclusions, cancellation terms and campus transport options. Do not claim preferred-hotel status, offer personal inducements, buy sponsorship on the assumption it secures room business, or displace the campus venue.

recommended_next_step.title: Recommended next step

Ask whether Roxanne Colthrust remains involved; use Veron Guy-Parks as an alternative administrative referral and Rhonda-Joy Lewis for routing if needed. Suggested positioning: “Could you direct us to the person coordinating accommodation for the 21–23 April 2027 conference? Spice Island would like to assess whether a limited suite allocation or small private hospitality event could fit your needs. Please confirm the sourcing process, permitted rate basis and transport requirements.” Only then prepare a tailored proposal with availability, inclusions, cancellation terms and campus transport options. Do not claim preferred-hotel status, offer personal inducements, buy sponsorship on the assumption it secures room business, or displace the campus venue.

potential_business.title: Potential business for this hotel
potential_business.body: Qualified prospect for selective accommodation and small ancillary hospitality, not the main conference venue. The announced meeting is on the SGU campus. Spice Island’s 64 luxury villa-style suites and all-inclusive beach-resort positioning suggest a possible fit for self-paying senior delegates, speakers or partner representatives whose travel policies allow it, plus optional pre/post stays. None of those segments is a confirmed booking. A small private dinner or reception is worth qualifying; the resort publishes wedding/event services for up to 35 guests, but that is not verified corporate meeting capacity. Do not assume the conference’s exhibition, catering or networking spend will move from campus to this hotel. Breakfast-only options merit discussion because delegates may spend conference days away from the resort.

facts_and_uncertainties.title: Established facts and uncertainties
facts: The official event site announces 21–23 April 2027, One Health, St. George’s University campus in Grenada, with CARPHA, the ministry and SGU as joint hosts.
The conference has advertised sponsorship and exhibition opportunities; the exhibition offer includes face-to-face delegate engagement and a coffee break in the exhibition area.
CARPHA reports preparatory discussions with SGU about conference logistics and stakeholder engagement.
Spice Island’s official accommodation inventory is 64 luxury villa-style suites; its resort page lists all-day dining with breakfast-only options available.
The resort advertises full-service wedding/event staff and catering for up to 35 guests in its wedding offer; no general conference capacity was established.
The accommodation page’s linked flyer is for the 2026 Guyana edition and must not be treated as a 2027 Grenada hotel list.
uncertainties: No verified hotel-sourcing or contracting decision-maker; all named contacts are planners, commercial-administration contacts, influencers or referrals rather than confirmed hotel buyers.
Roxanne Colthrust’s and Veron Guy-Parks’s documented conference responsibilities relate to 2026; continuation into 2027 is unconfirmed.
No verified 2027 attendance total, accommodation requirement, room-night commitment, budget, rate ceiling or Spice Island allocation.
No evidence that Spice Island is an official, preferred, overflow or contracted conference hotel.
No verified hotel meeting-room inventory, corporate-event capacity, date availability, accessible-suite specifications or campus transport arrangement.
No evidence of an incentive-travel component or a requirement for a resort-wide buyout.
